data.raw_text:
ICYMI O/N

MACRO:

Trump said he will meet with several parties over his ambition to take control of Greenland during the upcoming World Economic Forum. Trump said in a Truth Social post early Tuesday morning that he had a “very good telephone call” with Mark Rutte, the secretary general of NATO, concerning the Danish territory. (BBG)

Trump will deliver a special address to Davos at 2:30pm CET on Wednesday, according to his official schedule. (BBG)

Trump took a swipe at French leader Emmanuel Macron for rejecting an invitation to back his latest peace initiative and suggested he could impose a crushing tariff on champagne in retaliation. “I’ll put a 200% tariff on his wines and champagnes and he’ll join,” Trump said. (BBG)

Trump published a text message from French President Macron in which Macron invited Trump to have dinner in Paris on Thursday and to meet with Ukraine, Syria, Denmark and Russia. “I do not understand what you are doing on Greenland,” Macron told Trump in the text. (BBG)

US Treasury Secretary Bessent said President Trump could announce his pick for the next Federal Reserve chair as soon as next week. “We have four fantastic candidates — it will be up to the president, and I would imagine that he will have an announcement maybe as early as next week,” Bessent said in a press conference at Davos. (BBG)

Japan’s long-term government bond yields surged to multi-year highs Tuesday, spurred by fears that an upcoming election could lead to a consumption-tax rate cut that might worsen the country’s public finances. The yen and Nikkei saw selling pressure as a result. A consumption tax cut could cost around $31 billion annually in revenue, so how they are funded will be important for markets, an MUFG analyst said. (WSJ)

Macquarie Bank's analysts have suggested the BoJ may intervene as early as Wednesday to stop the rout in the nation’s bond market, “If the selloff continues, and especially if it spreads globally, then we should see BOJ dust [the bond buying tool] off and put it to work - maybe as early as tomorrow morning’s daily operations”. (BBG)

A meltdown in Japanese sovereign bonds, with yields on 40-year debt surging past 4% for the first time on record, may pile pressure on the Bank of Japan to act quicker to raise rates, according to some analysts. (BBG)

Japan’s chief government spokesperson played down the sudden meltdown in the Japanese bond market. “Long-term yields move on various factors and are determined in the market so I’ll refrain from commenting on every move, but we’re keeping a close eye on markets,” said government spokesperson Minoru Kihara on Tuesday. (BBG)

Japan’s 20-year government bond auction drew weaker demand than its 12-month average after government plans for tax relief on food jolted the debt market. (BBG)

Citigroup's analysts suggest the BoJ will potentially raise interest rates three times this year to double the current level if the yen’s weakness persists. Should the dollar rise above ¥160, the central bank is likely to lift the overnight call rate by a quarter of a percentage point to 1% in April, it said. (BBG)

Tourists to Japan hit a record high for the month of December despite the number of visitors from China plunging 45% due to diplomatic tensions between the two Asian neighbours. (RTRS)

Policymakers in Beijing are planning to boost Chinese domestic demand as part of their battle against entrenched deflationary pressures and plunging investment. Senior state planners are formulating a five year plan to lift domestic demand, acknowledging that the world’s second-largest economy currently faces an imbalance between “strong supply and weak demand,” according to comments from the NDRC to reporters. (WSJ)

China will keep the 2026 fiscal deficit and debt scale at levels deemed "necessary" and ensure an increase in the intensity of fiscal expenditure, Vice Finance Minister Liao Min said on Tuesday. Liao said at a press conference the country will channel more fiscal funds toward supporting consumption. (RTRS)

China will extend interest subsidies for consumers, service businesses and those in need of equipment upgrades to revive softening domestic demand, the country's finance ministry said on Tuesday. (RTRS)

China has announced incentives to spur investment and consumption, including a 500 billion-yuan loan guarantee facility to encourage private companies to borrow for expansion. (BBG)

China has purchased roughly 12 million tons of US soybeans in the last three months, clearing a closely watched trade hurdle and meeting a key pledge outlined by the Trump administration in November. (BBG)

China left benchmark loan prime rates unchanged on Tuesday for the eighth consecutive month in January, matching market expectations. (RTRS)

China, locked in a battle to lead technologies ranging from robotics to artificial intelligence, is studying whether to set up a national mergers and acquisition fund as Beijing ramps up its push for technological breakthroughs. (BBG)

Chinese exports of rare earth magnets to Japan in December fell 8% from November, when a diplomatic spat left market players concerned about future shipments. (RTRS)

China's yuan hit a fresh 32-month high against the dollar on Tuesday as the central bank's daily fixing neared the key 7.00 level, while seasonal settlement flows and greenback weakness helped to fuel the rally. (RTRS)

The last tankers carrying sanctioned Venezuelan crude to Asia are set to arrive in the coming days, effectively drawing to a close China’s easy access to a source of cheap oil that has helped sustain its refining sector. (BBG)

An Arctic blast is driving temperatures sharply lower across China this week, helping buoy liquefied natural gas prices and prompting authorities to issue warnings about freezing weather. (BBG)

'As U.S. orders fade, Chinese salespeople face tough grind in new markets' Reuters article notes how Chinese exporters are finding new markets to sell to but the compensation is not as great as the US was, creating struggles for many, highlighting it as a warning that Beijing relies too heavily on exports. (RTRS)

A corner of China’s credit market is signaling the country’s closer ties with Europe, with a record amount of bonds issued via a mechanism established by the Shanghai Clearing House and its counterpart in Brussels. (BBG)

Citigroup Inc. has downgraded European equities for the first time in over a year, citing worsening relations between Brussels and Washington over President Donald Trump’s push to seize Greenland. (BBG)

UK firms cut jobs at the fastest pace since 2020 and wage growth eased to its lowest in 3 1/2 years, more signs of a weakening jobs market as the Bank of England considers how much further it can cut interest rates. (BBG)

Rachel Reeves asks businesses to pitch UK as alternative to US at Davos. (FT)

The UK would be “foolish” to embrace the seemingly “simple solution” of a new customs union with the EU in an effort to boost economic growth, business secretary Peter Kyle has said despite growing fears of a trade war with Donald Trump. (FT)

Britain is considering a range of measures to better protect children online, including an Australian-style ban on social media for those below a certain age and tougher guidance for use of mobile phones in schools. (RTRS)

Australia's second-biggest pension fund says it is reducing its exposure to the U.S. dollar through currency hedging as falling interest rates and ongoing global volatility have investors around the world reassessing their U.S. allocations. (RTRS)

The South Korean Kospi Index’s stall shy of the 5,000 milestone reveals strains beneath the surface, as retail investors stay wary and gains hinge on just a handful of stocks. (BBG)

Taiwan aims to build a "democratic" high-tech supply chain with the United States and form a strategic AI partnership under the new tariffs deal it sealed with Washington last week, Taipei's top negotiator in the talks said on Tuesday. (RTRS)

Banks in Saudi Arabia are borrowing internationally at their fastest ever pace, as they rebalance their books after years fuelling the kingdom’s rapidly growing economy. (FT)

The Philippines started marketing its first dollar notes in a year, braving rocky markets. The bond sale will help raise dollars for the Philippines at a time when the peso is weakening, with the currency falling to a record low on Tuesday. (BBG) 

GEOPOLITICAL:

Trump criticized UK PM Starmer’s plans to return sovereignty of Diego Garcia — an island that houses a crucial military base — to Mauritius, reversing his previous support for the proposal in a further deterioration of transatlantic relations. Trump cited the decision to justify his ambitions for the US to acquire Greenland, in a post on Truth Social early Tuesday morning. (BBG)

The UK government is preparing to approve a contentious new Chinese “mega” embassy in London on Tuesday, after Britain’s intelligence services devised a range of protective security measures. (FT)

British and Chinese security officials established a forum to discuss cyberattacks following a spate of hacking accusations that soured relations between the two countries. (BBG)

Nigel Farage seeks meeting with UAE president to boost profile and build ties. (FT)

China has been invited to join U.S. President Donald Trump's Board of Peace initiative aimed at resolving global conflicts, a spokesperson at the Chinese foreign ministry said on Tuesday, without elaborating further. (RTRS)

Militant group Islamic State claimed an explosion that officials said killed a Chinese national and six Afghans, while injuring several more as it tore through a Chinese-run restaurant in a heavily guarded part of Afghanistan's capital. (RTRS)

EQUITIES:

Nvidia and AMD graphics cards have seen 15%-20% price hikes over the past 2-weeks due to rising memory chip prices, media report, citing Taiwan distributors. (CTEE via @dnystedt)

GFHK’s analyst Jeff Pu reportedly suggests Meta is scaling back its in-house ASIC (MTIA) plans, and instead of buying TPUs, it’s buying AMD’s MI455X. (unconfirmed; via @jukan05)

'Chevron’s Dilemma in Venezuela: Support Trump’s Vision Without Losing Money' WSJ articloe notes how Chevron has expressed caution for further investment in Venezuela, showing how far Trump’s aspirations for a speedy Venezuelan oil revival are from what the U.S. oil industry considers to be realistic. (WSJ)

Lululemon founder Chip Wilson is trying to excise private equity firm Advent from the apparel maker's board as part of an ongoing proxy fight, according to Semafor sources. (Semafor)

Elliott Investment Management has made an investment in Stratolaunch, a privately held hypersonic-flight company, according to WSJ sources. (WSJ)

Taiwan's Inventec President Jack Tsai said the decision on Nvidia's H200 artificial intelligence chips "appears to be stuck on the China side," he told a press conference in Taipei on Tuesday. (RTRS)

Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix, which together hold more than 60% of the global NAND flash market, are expected to reduce their NAND flash production this year. (Chosun via @jukan05)

ByteDance is making an aggressive push into China’s cloud market, as the TikTok owner seeks to use its AI advances to diversify beyond the consumer apps that have powered its rise, according to FT sources. The strategy is disrupting a multibillion-dollar industry that has been long dominated by Alibaba, Tencent and Huawei. (FT)

Baidu’s AI assistant has surpassed 200 million monthly active users after its launch in 2023, according to WSJ sources, as competition intensifies among Chinese tech giants in the AI field. Last week Alibaba annonced its Qwen app surpassed 100mln MAUs within two months of its November launch. (WSJ)

China has broadened a probe into PDD Holdings Inc. after its employees exchanged blows with regulators, dispatching over 100 investigators from various agencies to the company’s Shanghai headquarters in recent weeks, according to Bloomberg sources. (BBG)

'Chinese automakers take aim at UK to supercharge global EV ambitions' FT article notes how Nio, Aion and Zeekr are set to launch in the UK this year, becoming the latest Chinese carmakers to use Europe’s second-largest electric vehicle market to test their global ambitions. (FT)

Pop Mart International Group Ltd. shares soared the most in five months after the Chinese toymaker’s first share buyback since 2024 boosted investor confidence. (BBG)

Shares of China Tourism Group Duty Free rose after the company said it plans to acquire LVMH’s DFS travel retail business in Hong Kong and Macau. (WSJ)

GSK has reached an agreement to acquire Rapt Therapeutics, a US-based biotech developing therapies for treating people with inflammatory and immunologic diseases, in a deal that values the company at $2.2bn. (FT)

The online brawl between Elon Musk and Ryanair Holdings Plc dragged into a second week, with the world’s richest man again floating the idea of buying the airline after clashing with its chief executive officer. (BBG)

New carbon tax will hurt British industry say steel, cement and chemicals groups. (FT)

Wise Plc said it’s on track to shift its primary listing to the US in the first half of this year, as continued customer growth fueled a 21% increase in underlying income in the third quarter. (BBG)

Henkel said it was in discussions with the majority owner of Stahl Holdings over a potential acquisition of the Dutch specialty-chemicals company. (WSJ)

BHP Group upgraded its annual copper-production guidance amid record-high prices for the industrial metal, but announced another cost overrun on its giant potash project in Canada. (WSJ)

(BBG) Japan’s long-term government bond yields surged to multi-year highs Tuesday, spurred by fears that an upcoming election could lead to a consumption-tax rate cut that might worsen the country’s public finances. (BBG) Citigroup's analysts suggest the BoJ will potentially raise interest rates three times this year to double the current level if the yen’s weakness persists. (BBG) China left benchmark loan prime rates unchanged on Tuesday for the eighth consecutive month in January, matching market expectations.
